narrative:
Based on your application, the model estimated a 43% chance that you would become a credit risk, meaning the bank saw a materially higher likelihood of non-payment than it can accept. While that also means a 57% chance you would repay, the elevated risk was enough to deny the loan.

The three most important factors in that decision were, in order: the amount you requested, the balance in your checking account, and your credit history. Interestingly, the requested amount—3,804 DM, higher than the average approved loan of about 3,020 DM—was not what hurt you. In fact, this factor nudged the decision toward approving you. So asking for that amount alone was not the problem.

The bigger concerns were your checking account and your credit history. Your checking account had a balance between 0 and 200 DM, a range that appears in only around 18% of approved applicants. Many approved borrowers had no checking account at all or a more comfortable balance, so this modest amount gave the model little confidence in your financial cushion.

Your credit history was the clearest warning sign. You have no existing credits and have paid all past debts, but among approved borrowers, this profile is extremely rare—only about 1%. Lenders prefer to see a proven record of managing credit, such as previously paid loans. The absence of that track record made it hard for the model to see you as a reliable borrower.

To improve your chances next time, focus on building a stronger credit history: open a credit card or small installment loan, pay it consistently over time, and keep a larger buffer in your checking account before reapplying.
